data.hypothesis: A 512-CTA cap gives twice the CTA-level parallelism of the previously tested 256 cap while halving the atomic count of the 1024-cap candidate. Four independent per-thread accumulators may reduce long serial accumulation chains and loop overhead, potentially recovering input-streaming throughput without increasing CTA atomics beyond 512. The controller must measure total time including the default-stream reset and launch, and validate all required sizes, seeds, repeated calls, and FP64 tolerance.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this single-kernel CTA-atomic approach, the measured 256-CTA cap was slower than the measured 1024-CTA cap, so fewer atomics alone did not establish a faster total call. An intermediate cap with a different per-thread accumulation pattern tests whether parallelism and accumulation overhead explain the contrast.
memory_lessons.claim: The 1024-cap candidate was valid at 0.0004473899 s mean, while the 256-cap candidate was valid at 0.0015542955 s mean; the smaller cap did not improve total time in those trials.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the 512-cap, four-accumulator kernel with reset and launch included, then compare against both prior atomic candidates and the baseline across all correctness cases.

data.notes: This candidate resets output on every call in the default stream, then reads input once in a fused kernel and performs one output atomic per CTA; scratch is unused. Existing measurements show the 1024-cap candidate at 0.0004473899 s mean, the 256-cap candidate at 0.0015542955 s, and the two-stage baseline at 0.0012280939 s. The new candidate is unmeasured; these results do not predict its performance. Controller validation should include all required sizes and seeds, repeated calls, and the FP64 tolerance.
transformations: Replace the two-kernel scratch-based reduction with a fused single-kernel absolute-value reduction and one output atomic per CTA.
Process four grid-stride positions per loop iteration into independent per-thread accumulators before the CUB block reduction.
Choose ceil(n/256) CTAs for smaller inputs and cap the grid at 512 CTAs for larger inputs.
Reset the output asynchronously on every call before launching the kernel; do not depend on scratch contents.
